metadata.name: Ecodesign for Swift
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Swift code: battery-aware background work, reused sessions, streamed data, no blocking of the main thread.

energie.name: Swift — device energy
energie.description: On a phone the energy is the user's battery, and the sensors are the expensive part (RGESN UX/Algorithms).

rules.title: Sensor left running
rules.description: Location, motion and Bluetooth scanning keep power-hungry hardware awake. Started and never stopped, they drain a battery in the background for a screen the user closed an hour ago.
rules.recommendation: Stop the updates as soon as the screen or the task that needed them goes away, ask for the coarsest accuracy that works, and prefer significant-change monitoring over continuous updates.
rules.note: One stop call anywhere in the file silences the rule. That is usually right, since start and stop are normally written as a pair, but a file starting several sensors needs each one stopped.

rules.title: Timer used to poll
rules.description: A repeating timer that re-fetches state runs whether or not anything changed, wakes the radio, and prevents the device from settling into a low-power state.
rules.recommendation: Drive the refresh from an event: a push notification, a WebSocket, a delegate callback. Where a timer is unavoidable, invalidate it when the view disappears and widen the interval.
rules.note: One invalidate() anywhere in the file silences the rule. Check that the timer flagged here is the one being invalidated, and that it happens when the view goes away.

ressources.name: Swift — resources and I/O
ressources.description: Reuse sessions, stream large data, keep the main thread free (RGESN Backend/Frontend).

rules.title: Main thread blocked
rules.description: A synchronous wait on the main thread freezes the interface: nothing renders, nothing responds, and the user taps again, which queues more work for the same result.
rules.recommendation: Keep the main thread for the interface. Move the work to a background queue or an async task, and update the UI when it returns.

example.good: Task { let d = await load(); await MainActor.run { render(d) } }

rules.title: Whole file or response held in memory
rules.description: Data(contentsOf:) loads everything before anything can be used. On a large download that is a memory spike, and on a slow connection it is a wait with nothing on screen.
rules.recommendation: Use URLSession download or stream tasks, decode incrementally, and bound what you keep.

rules.title: URLSession built per request
rules.description: A session created for each call loses its connection pool and its cache: every request redoes DNS and the TLS handshake, on a radio that costs more energy the longer it stays awake.
rules.recommendation: Share one session for the app or the service, configured once with its cache policy and timeouts.
rules.note: A session held in a static let or a lazy var is exactly the recommendation, so the rule stays silent as soon as the file declares one.
